title: Quality monitoring call
respondents: Every person we support, at least every 3 months, by phone or at a face-to-face quality visit; a representative answers only where the person cannot give their views, even with support
summary: The quality check every person has at least every 3 months: the core questions shared with the annual survey, staff understanding them, contacting the office, medicines where we help, anything to change and thanks to pass on. Named, interviewer-led, about 13 minutes.
purpose: The quality check the Compliments, Feedback and Involvement Procedure requires for every person at least every 3 months: a phone call by a Care Coordinator, or a private face-to-face visit by a Field Care Supervisor for people at higher risk, never by the core care team. It is our most frequent structured contact with everyone we support and the way we hear from people who will never fill in a form. It asks the standard question set in the same words as the annual survey (overall experience, on time, visit length, familiar care workers, care given your way, doing what matters, dignity, fair treatment, culture and beliefs, feeling safe, our information and telling us if unhappy), plus whether care workers understand the person and whether they know how to contact the office, anything they would change and any compliment to pass on; and, where we help with medicines, whether help comes at the right times and anything has gone wrong. Results feed quality check satisfaction and calls on time on the quality dashboard, the monthly feedback summary, the annual equality review and the communication monitoring of the Communication and Accessible Information Policy. It evidences Regulation 17(2)(a) and (e), Regulation 9(3) and Regulation 16(2), and people's experience under all five CQC key questions.

timing.when: At least every 3 months for each person, staggered across the quarter; a phone call, or a private face-to-face visit for people at higher risk
timing.trigger: The person's quality check falling due (at least every 3 months)

introduction:
This call from {{organisation}} is to check your care is right for you. It takes about 13 minutes. You can tell me anything, good or bad: some people tell us things that could be better, and we want to hear it. What you say will not affect your care.

Your answers are linked to your name so we can sort out anything that is not right. Your care workers (carers) will not see them.

This survey is not for urgent concerns. If you are worried about your safety or someone else's, or need help now, phone the office (out of hours, the on-call number in your care folder). In an emergency, call 999.
privacyNotice:
{{organisation}} uses your answers to check your care is right for you and to improve our service. The law expects us to ask for feedback; our legal reason for using your answers is our legitimate interest in running a good, safe service. Health details stay confidential.

Your answers are linked to your name so we can put things right. They are seen only by our Registered Manager, Deputy Manager, safeguarding lead, Care Coordinators and Field Care Supervisors, never by your care workers (carers), and reports show combined results only. If you tell us someone may be at risk of harm, we may tell the council to keep them safe.

We keep your answers for 3 years after this check, under our Records Management and Retention Policy. You can ask to see, correct or delete your answers, or object to our using them. To do this, or to complain about how we use your information, contact the office or our Data Protection Officer (details on our website). You can also complain to the Information Commission.

questions.text: Overall, how was your experience of our service?
questions.helpText: Please think about your care since we last spoke. Choose "Don't know" if you are not sure.

comment.prompt: Please tell us why you gave this answer.

questions.text: Do your care workers arrive on time?
questions.helpText: On time means within about half an hour of the time agreed with you.

comment.prompt: Please tell us more, for example which visits are late.

questions.text: Do your care workers stay for the time agreed for your visit?
questions.helpText: For example, if your visit is booked for 45 minutes, do they stay that long, unless you ask them to go earlier?

comment.prompt: Please tell us more, for example which visits are cut short.

questions.text: Are you visited by care workers you know?
questions.helpText: We mean your regular care workers, or new ones who have been introduced to you.
questions.evidence: Responsive: Care provision, integration and continuity

comment.prompt: Please tell us more, for example how often someone new comes.

questions.text: Do your care workers do things the way you want them done?
questions.helpText: For example, asking you first and listening to how you like things done.

comment.prompt: Please tell us what you would like done differently.

questions.text: Does our care help you do the things that matter to you?
questions.helpText: For example, staying in your own home, getting up and dressed, or seeing family and friends.

comment.prompt: What would help you do more of the things that matter to you?

questions.text: Do your care workers treat you with dignity and respect?
questions.helpText: For example, keeping you covered during personal care and taking care of your home.

questions.text: Do you feel we treat you fairly?
questions.helpText: Fairly means giving you care as good as anyone else gets, whatever your age, disability, race, religion, sex or sexuality.
questions.evidence: Responsive: Equity in experiences and outcomes

questions.text: Do your care workers respect your culture and beliefs?
questions.helpText: For example, your religion, your language, the food you eat, how you like to dress, or anything else about who you are. Choose "Does not apply to me" if this does not matter to you.

comment.prompt: Please tell us what we could do differently.

sections.title: Feeling safe

questions.text: Do you feel safe with your care workers?
questions.helpText: If you do not feel safe, please do not wait for this survey. Phone the office now, or call 999 in an emergency.

comment.prompt: Please tell us what would help you feel safer.

sections.introduction: You can skip this question if you would rather not answer it.

questions.text: Do your care workers understand what you tell them?
questions.helpText: Think about the words, signs, language or aids you use to communicate.

comment.prompt: What would help them understand you?

questions.text: Is the information we give you easy for you to use?
questions.helpText: For example, letters, your care plan and your list of visit times. We can give you information in large print, easy read, audio or another language.

comment.prompt: What would make our information easier for you?

questions.text: Do we help you with your medicines?
questions.helpText: For example, reminding you, handing you your medicines, or giving them to you.

questions.text: Do you get help with your medicines at the right times?
questions.helpText: For example, before food, or at the times your doctor or pharmacist said. Choose "Don't know" if you are not sure what times your medicines should be taken.

comment.prompt: Please tell us which medicines or times.

questions.text: Since we last spoke, has anything gone wrong when care workers helped with your medicines?
questions.helpText: For example, a medicine was missed, given at the wrong time, or the wrong one was given.

comment.prompt: Please tell us what happened and when.

questions.text: Do you know how to contact our office, including evenings and weekends?
questions.helpText: The numbers are in your welcome pack and care folder.

questions.text: If you were unhappy with your care, would you feel able to tell us?
questions.helpText: This includes making a complaint. Choose "Don't know" if you are not sure.
options: Yes, but I am not sure how
questions.evidence: Responsive: Listening to and involving people

comment.prompt: What would make it easier to tell us?

questions.text: Is there anything about your care you would like us to change?
questions.helpText: For example, visit times, which care workers come, or how things are done.

questions.text: Is there anything your care workers do that you would like us to thank them for?
questions.helpText: We will pass your thanks on to them. You can name them if you wish.

questions.text: For the interviewer: what did you observe about the person's wellbeing?
questions.helpText: Not read out. Complete it whenever a representative answered for the person, and note anything that worried you.

questions.text: Would you like someone to contact you about your answers?
questions.helpText: If you choose Yes, someone from our office, not one of your care workers, will contact you within 5 working days.

howToRun: Every person has this check at least every 3 months, staggered across the quarter: a phone call by a Care Coordinator, or, for people who live alone, have dementia or other cognitive impairment, have communication difficulties or have no family or representative involved, a private face-to-face visit by a Field Care Supervisor, combined with a spot check where possible but held away from the care worker and never during personal care. It is never carried out by a member of the person's core care team.

Quality checks are calls and visits, so they are recorded, not sent; CareFlow does not track each person's due date. Each quarter start a copy from this template (for example "Quality calls, January to March") and use Open for responses; enter every call or visit with Record response, channel Telephone or In person, on the day. Keep a list of everyone we support with the date of their last check, and each week the Care Coordinator checks it for due and overdue checks: a check more than 2 weeks overdue is an action trigger in the Compliments, Feedback and Involvement Procedure. By default only managers and admins can record survey answers ("Record survey responses") and only managers can open a survey for responses: give both permissions to the Care Coordinators and Field Care Supervisors who make the checks, who can otherwise only view surveys.

Read each question, its help text and every answer choice exactly as written, slowly; pause and repeat when asked, and offer breaks or a second call (save the answers only after the last call: CareFlow accepts one answer from each person). Reading every choice aloud is why it takes about 13 minutes. A large print or easy read card with three answers (Always or usually; Sometimes; Rarely or never) may be left at a visit. Ask the medicines questions only where we help with medicines.

Ask the dignity and feeling safe questions only once the person confirms they can talk privately; otherwise leave them unanswered, note "not asked: not private" in the call notes, and the Field Care Supervisor asks them privately at the next spot check, as the Compliments, Feedback and Involvement Procedure sets. Use a professional interpreter, never a family member.

A representative answers only where the person cannot give their views even with support: record them in CareFlow's "Who is answering" field and complete the interviewer's observation question. Report representatives' answers separately.

If the person cannot be reached, try three times at different times of day over 5 working days; then the Field Care Supervisor completes the check face to face within the next 10 working days. A person may decline: record it in their care plan, offer again at the next care plan review, and still invite them to the annual survey.

This check is the person's survey contact for its 4 weeks: before the call, check the person's survey history in CareFlow and do not ask the monthly visit check-in within 4 weeks either side. A check due in February is done in early January, or with the annual survey in the same call.

Use the same words as the annual survey for the shared questions: never reword them, so results compare. Feedback for a care worker's appraisal is collected at the same visit with the separate appraisal feedback survey (SUR-PWS-020), never by the care worker being appraised.

Who may open individual answers: the Care Coordinators and Field Care Supervisors who make the checks, and the managers. This is set in Who can see the answers: individual responses are limited to Care Coordinators, Field Care Supervisors, the Registered Manager, the Deputy Manager and the safeguarding lead, and results to the same staff, showing from 5 answers. Super Admin, Admin and the person who made the survey can always see both, so keep those roles to staff who may open them.
actingOnResults: The person making the check acts on every answer that needs action the same working day under the alerts below, and records any change in the care plan or daily visit notes.

How to count: quality check satisfaction is the share answering Very good or Good to the overall question, leaving out Don't know (dashboard target at least 90%; checks on time target 100%). For the other scale questions report the share answering Always or Usually, leaving out Does not apply to me and Don't know, and for raising concerns the share answering Yes, and I know how. The medicines questions are asked only where we help with medicines: report them with that base. Always show how many people answered, and report phone, visit and representative answers separately.

The Deputy Manager's monthly feedback summary to the Monthly Quality and Governance Meeting reports checks on time, satisfaction and comment themes from the fixed theme list. Satisfaction below 90% in any branch, the same negative theme from 3 or more people in one branch in a month, or any check more than 2 weeks overdue needs action: the Registered Manager records the reason and an action in the service improvement plan under the Governance and Quality Assurance Policy. Themes that show a training need go to the training lead.

The fairness and culture results go to the annual equality review under the Equality, Diversity and Human Rights in Care Policy, and the understanding and information results to the communication monitoring under the Communication and Accessible Information Policy. Never report a group of fewer than 5 people separately, and flag results resting on fewer than 10.

Keep individual answers for 3 years after the check under the Records Management and Retention Policy. For CQC, the named, dated check records with people's own words, the monthly summaries and the actions taken are evidence of seeking and acting on feedback (Regulation 17(2)(e)) and of people's experience under each key question.

alerts.when: "Do you feel safe with your care workers?" answered Sometimes, Rarely or Never, or any comment or observation suggesting abuse, neglect or that someone is at risk.
alerts.action: Treat as a possible safeguarding concern. Call 999 first if anyone is in immediate danger. Pass it to the safeguarding lead the same working day; the lead assesses the risk within 1 hour, arranges a private conversation with the person by someone outside their core care team, and refers to the local authority where needed, immediately if the risk is immediate and otherwise the same working day, under the Safeguarding Concerns: Reporting, Referral and Enquiry Procedure. A concern about a member of staff also follows the Managing Allegations Against Staff Procedure.

rule.task: Possible safeguarding concern: does not always feel safe

alerts.when: "Do you feel safe with your care workers?" answered Usually, or the safety or dignity question not asked because the person could not talk privately.
alerts.action: The Field Care Supervisor asks privately at the next spot check and records the answer; for Usually, the Care Coordinator also contacts the person within 5 working days, once they can talk privately, to ask what would help them feel safer.

rule.task: Ask privately what would help them feel safer

alerts.when: "Do your care workers treat you with dignity and respect?", "Do your care workers respect your culture and beliefs?" or "Do you feel we treat you fairly?" answered Rarely or Never, or a comment describing unfair or degrading treatment.
alerts.action: Tell the Registered Manager the same working day. Dissatisfaction is a complaint, recorded the same working day under the Complaints Policy and Procedure; discrimination by our staff is graded High and the Registered Manager decides within 1 hour whether it is a safeguarding concern, under the Equality, Diversity and Human Rights in Care Policy. Degrading or humiliating treatment goes straight to the safeguarding lead.

alerts.when: "Since we last spoke, has anything gone wrong when care workers helped with your medicines?" answered Yes or Not sure, or "Do you get help with your medicines at the right times?" answered Rarely or Never.
alerts.action: Check the eMAR and log any medicines problem in the incident log the same working day under the Medication Errors, Near Misses and Incidents Procedure. The Registered Manager or Deputy Manager decides within 1 hour what keeps the person safe until the next visit; where the medicine is time-sensitive or a dose is due today, phone the person at once and get advice from their GP or pharmacist.

rule.task: Possible medicines problem: check the eMAR and log it

alerts.when: "Do your care workers arrive on time?", "Do your care workers stay for the time agreed for your visit?" or "Are you visited by care workers you know?" answered Rarely or Never, or a comment describing a missed visit.
alerts.action: The Care Coordinator checks the check-in and check-out records and continuity for the last 3 months within 5 working days and agrees changes with the person. A missed visit not already recorded goes in the incident log the same working day, graded at least Medium, under the Missed, Late and Short Visits Procedure.

alerts.when: "Do your care workers understand what you tell them?" or "Is the information we give you easy for you to use?" answered Rarely or Never.
alerts.action: The Care Coordinator contacts the person within 5 working days; a new or changed communication need is recorded the same working day and the agreed format or support put in place within 5 working days, under the Communication and Accessible Information Policy.

rule.task: Communication need: agree format or support

alerts.when: "Do you know how to contact our office, including evenings and weekends?" answered No or Not sure, or "If you were unhappy with your care, would you feel able to tell us?" answered "Yes, but I am not sure how", No or Don't know.
alerts.action: Give the numbers during the call and re-send them, with the How to raise a concern or make a complaint leaflet, in the person's recorded format within 5 working days. For No to telling us, a Field Care Supervisor outside the core care team offers a private conversation and the details of the local independent advocacy service.

rule.task: Re-send office numbers and the complaints leaflet

if.question: q-tell-us
answers: Yes, but I am not sure how

alerts.when: Overall experience answered Poor or Very poor, or any other question answered Rarely or Never, with no particular concern described; or a comment expressing dissatisfaction that needs a response.
alerts.action: Pass it to the Care Coordinator the same working day, who contacts the person within 5 working days. Dissatisfaction that needs a response is a complaint: record it the same working day, grade it within 1 working day and acknowledge it within 3 working days under the Complaints Policy and Procedure. If unsure, treat it as a complaint.

alerts.when: An answer to "Is there anything about your care you would like us to change?" asking for a change.
alerts.action: Acknowledge it to the person by the end of the next working day; a permanent change to visit times or tasks is decided and confirmed within 5 working days, under the Person-Centred Care, Dignity and Respect Policy.

alerts.when: The interviewer observes a decline in the person's wellbeing or abilities.
alerts.action: The Care Coordinator decides the same working day whether a care plan review is needed, under the Care Plan Review Procedure.

alerts.when: "Would you like someone to contact you about your answers?" answered Yes.
alerts.action: The Care Coordinator, or someone else outside the person's core care team, contacts the person within 5 working days in the way they prefer and records what was agreed.

rule.task: Asked to be contacted about their answers

alerts.when: An answer to "Is there anything your care workers do that you would like us to thank them for?", or any other comment praising our service or a named member of staff.
alerts.action: Record it as a compliment in CareFlow the same working day; the Field Care Supervisor or line manager passes it to each employee named within 5 working days, under the Compliments, Feedback and Involvement Procedure.

regulatoryBasis.source: Health and Social Care Act 2008 (Regulated Activities) Regulations 2014, Regulation 17(2)(a) and (e): assess, monitor and improve quality, including people's experience; seek and act on feedback
Health and Social Care Act 2008 (Regulated Activities) Regulations 2014, Regulation 9(3): involving people in decisions about their care
Health and Social Care Act 2008 (Regulated Activities) Regulations 2014, Regulation 16(2): an accessible system for identifying, receiving and handling complaints

NICE NG21 Home care, recommendations 1.1.3 (regularly seek feedback, including from people who have no carer or advocate), 1.4.9 (independent advocacy) and 1.7.7 (use people's feedback to assess training needs)

NHS England, Using the Friends and Family Test to improve patient experience (version 2): asking at regular intervals during ongoing care needs careful engagement for honest feedback; supported answering follows the Mental Capacity Act
Mental Capacity Act 2005, section 1(2) and (3): presume capacity and take all practicable steps to help a person decide
